rule: Server sends absolute galactic time (ServerTime every 60 s by the donor's own doc, and at scene start). The client stores the time and the local clock at receipt. Each frame: now = stored time + (local clock minus stored local clock) times test scale; wrapped by planet cycle (header TimeCycle, else 3600 s); plus a phase offset; fraction 0..1 maps to an hour angle on two spans: night from sunset to sunrise (0.36 of cycle by default) and day for the rest (0.64). Sun direction, sky ramp and fog follow from that angle.
keep: Server owns absolute time; client extrapolates between syncs
Cycle wrap and a phase offset per zone
Two fractions (sunset, sunrise) set night and day lengths, so a long dusk is a data knob
Weather as a row per weather state from one table
change: Ease the re-anchor over about 2 s, or add half the round trip (E1)
Test scale 60 must not snap every sync (E1)
Help text and sphere agree: noon as computed, or phase offset moved (E2)
Fallback cycle as a named constant; comment corrected (E3)
Spawns and any timed event decided on the server from the same clock; the sky is client-only
Wire the weather message and select the row by state (W1)
look_test: One zone, day clock at test scale 60 for three minutes with the 60 s sync. Version A snaps back each minute (donor behaviour). Version B eases over 2 s. Dom watches the sunset on a phone and judges whether dusk reads as a warning for a night event, and whether the snap breaks it.
